data.description:
## Problem

A normal LLM code review with inline comments dispatches one Gerrit Verified workflow per review event for the same unchanged patchset. The redundant runs cancel useful in-flight jobs through the `gerrit-verify-rebar~<change>` concurrency group, queue behind one another, consume scarce runners, and can replace a valid test result with cancellation noise.

## Observed evidence

On Gerrit change 2225 patchset 6, canonical Verified run 32926871119 started at 2026-08-26T03:33:08Z. The review bot published four inline comments plus its final vote around 03:42-03:43Z. GitHub then received workflow_dispatch runs 32927478228 (03:42:48), 32927480722 (03:42:50), 32927483100 (03:42:52), 32927485234 (03:42:54), and 32927544184 (03:43:48), all for the unchanged change. Run 32926871119 reported: `Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for gerrit-verify-rebar~2225 exists`, canceling its bounded mutation shard after 8m45s. This was not an operator recheck.

Related precedent `musophobic-secondary-jaguar` fixed the narrower `recheck-review` ChatOps word collision; this occurrence is ordinary review publication and therefore a distinct trigger/filter defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new patchset dispatches exactly one canonical Verified run.
- [ ] Review-bot inline comments and LLM-Review label votes do not dispatch or supersede Verified runs.
- [ ] The authorized CI recheck mechanism still dispatches exactly one replacement run.
- [ ] Tests replay a review containing multiple inline comments plus a final vote and assert zero additional Verified dispatches.
- [ ] Diagnostics identify the Gerrit event type and deduplication key when a dispatch is accepted or suppressed.
- [ ] The fix preserves Gerrit change/patchset scoping and does not broaden concurrency across unrelated changes.
data.title: LLM review comments dispatch duplicate Gerrit Verified runs
